AI Readiness Self-Assessment Ten statements. Answer honestly.

Ten statements about your AI estate, meaning every AI system you run, whether bought or built. Your answers stay on your device and there is no form at the end.

3 MINUTESNOTHING IS SENTNO EMAIL REQUIRED
The assessment

Answer for the estate, not for your best system.

Score the organization as a whole. Scoring only your strongest system gives a comfortable result that tells you little.

We hold a current inventory of every AI system in use, including the ones bought as a feature of something else.

For each system we can say whether it touches personal data, and under which jurisdiction.

We can name the person who approved each system running in production.

We can produce the information that person had at the time they approved it.

Every system that acts without asking has a written limit and somebody who reads the log.

We have halted an AI system on purpose, in production, and know how long it took.

Model or system performance has been tested on our own data, not the vendor’s benchmark.

Someone outside the team that built or runs the system has tested whether it works.

We could assemble an evidence pack for our main obligation in under a week.

The last governance review changed something we can point at.

READINESS0 / 10 ANSWERED
— / 10
ANSWER THREE TO SEE A LEVEL

Each statement is either true of your organization today or it is not. Partly counts as half. In practice, partly is where most of the risk lives.

A low score is the normal result, and it is the useful one.

Every organization we assess has policies. Far fewer can produce the artifacts on this list at speed. If you scored below five, you are in ordinary company, and you now know which statements to fix first. The AI Estate Inventory engagement starts with the first two: a complete register of every AI system you run, with the data it touches and the jurisdiction it falls under.
